POLICE HEADQUARTERS,
HONG KONG.

CONFIDENTIAL.

22nd. December, 1932.

Sir,

I have the honour to enclose a copy of
a letter from Mrs. H.V. Mc.Dougall, in which she
enquires after her brother Eardley Thomas Maitland
who was subject of your letter No.D.3466 of the 14th
April, 1932. The last the Police here heard of
Maitland is that he left for Shanghai per s.s."Tanda"
on the 5th August, 1932. If you have any later
information about him, perhaps you would communicate
with Mrs. Mc.Dougall.

I have the honour to be,
Sir,
Your obedient servant,

O'Leary
Director, Criminal Intelligence.

Maitland called here about
2 months ago intended to write
home to his sister. No further action
seems required. J.W.O. Davidson 5/1/33
The Deputy Commissioner of Crime (Special Branch),
Shanghai Municipal Council,
SHANGHAI.

（批：For Davidson
HBM C. Genl

先生，

谨随函附上 H.V. 麦克杜格尔夫人 (Mrs. H.V. Mc.Dougall) 来信副本一份，她在信中询问其兄厄德利·托马斯·梅特兰 (Eardley Thomas Maitland) 的近况，此人即贵处1932年4月14日第 D.3466 号信函所涉之人。本处警方最后获悉关于梅特兰的消息是，他于1932年8月5日乘“坦达”号轮船 (s.s. "Tanda") 前往上海。若贵处有关于他的最新信息，或许请与麦克杜格尔夫人联系。

谨此致意，
先生，
您顺从的仆人，

奥莱利 (O'Leary)

COPY.

38 Cambridge Street,
Hyde Park,
London, W.2.

The Chief of the Police,
Hong Kong.

Dear Sir,

I shall be deeply grateful for all the information
you can give me concerning my brother Eardley Thomas Maitland,
B.A., late of Shanghai. I was informed that he was at
Station House, 59, Nathan Road, Kowloon, Hong Kong, China.
I heard indirectly he was believed to be in want. I cabled
£20, twenty pounds, to him and the receipt which has come
back appears to have been signed by him. I cabled out a
reply paid cable, a cable came back that he was writing.
This was June 30th, 1932. I have written to him and all
letters have been returned marked " not here". I have had
no written communication from him for the last two years.
I am anxious to help him if he needs help and there is no
reason for him to be short of any money he needs, if he will
only write and prove his identity,

There has been so much mystery that my solicitor
says we must have proof of his being alive and of course I am
most anxious to know all.

Do please say everything you know and advise me what
to do for the best for him.

Thanking you in anticipation for all the trouble
you may take on my behalf.

Yours faithfully,

(Sd.) Helena Victoria A. Mc.Dougall,
nee Maitland.

副本。

伦敦 W.2，海德公园，
剑桥街 38 号。

致：
香港警察总监。

尊敬的先生：

对于您能提供的有关我兄长、文学士、前居上海的厄德利·托马斯·梅特兰 (Eardley Thomas Maitland) 的一切信息，我将深表感激。我得知他曾在中国香港九龙弥敦道 59 号的警署 (Station House)。我间接听说据信他生活困窘。我曾给他汇去 20 英镑，退回的收据上似乎有他的签名。我曾发去一封由收方付费的电报，回电称他正在写信。那是1932年6月30日。我曾去信给他，但所有信件均被退回，并注明“此人不在该址”。过去两年里，我没有收到过他的任何书面通信。如果他需要帮助，我很乐意相助；只要他肯写信并证明其身份，他没有理由缺钱花。

由于疑团重重，我的律师说我们必须有他还活着的证明，当然我也迫切希望了解一切。

恳请告知您所知道的一切情况，并就如何对他最为有利向我提供建议。

预先感谢您为我费心。

您忠实的，

(签名) 海伦娜·维多利亚·A·麦克杜格尔 (Helena Victoria A. Mc.Dougall)，
娘家姓梅特兰。

D. 3466

April 14, 32.

Secret and
Confidential.

Sir,

Mr. E. T. Maitland

I have the honour to acknowledge receipt
of your letter, C.I.D. No. 924/31 of April 2
and in reply to inform you that the person
mentioned above was Prosecuting Solicitor to the
Shanghai Municipal Police from December 1922 to
November 1928 when his agreement was terminated
whilst on long leave in Europe. He returned
to Shanghai the same year and established a law
practice locally.

He was at various times connected with clubs
of doubtful reputation in regard to gambling.
Police reports indicate that he was also interested
in slot machines and in this connection I would
refer you to my confidential letter No. I.O. D. 42
of January 25, 1929.

I have the honour to be,
Sir,
Your Obedient Servant,

Deputy Commissioner
(Crime Branch)

The Inspector-General of Police,
HONGKONG.

先生，

E. T. 梅特兰先生

谨此确认收到贵处4月2日
刑事侦缉处编号 924/31 来信，
现回复如下：上述人士曾于1922年12月至
1928年11月期间担任上海公共租界警务处
公诉律师，其间他在欧洲长期休假时
合同被终止。同年他返回
上海，并在当地开设了一家律师事务所。

他在不同时期与一些在赌博方面
声誉不佳的俱乐部有关联。
警方报告表明，他对老虎机也感兴趣，
就此事项，请参阅我1929年1月25日的
机密信函，编号 I.O. D. 42。

谨此致意，
先生，
您顺从的仆人，

副警务处长
(罪案股)

致：
香港警务总监。

POLICE HEADQUARTERS,
HONG KONG.

CID No. 924/31.
2nd April 1932.

Sir,

I have the honour to inform you that a certain
EARDLEY THOMAS MAITLAND, who formerly practised as a
solicitor in Shanghai, is now in Hong Kong. I have
received information that he is thinking of joining a
firm of solicitors here.

I shall be glad, therefore, if you will let me
know if you have any information of interesting concerning
his previous history.

I have the honour to be,
Sir,
Your obedient servant,

p. Inspector General of Police.

The Deputy Commissioner of Crime (Special Branch),
Shanghai Municipal Police,
SHANGHAI.
